sections.heading: Wiring Added to a Home So It Looks Like It Was Always There
body: If your existing home needs additional electrical wiring, our aim is to make it look as if it was always there. That covers added outlets in a house, a garage or a shed.
We know your home is more than just a house. Whether you're starting over or adding to your current residence, we'll make sure it's still home sweet home.

sections.heading: Family Owned, With a Smaller Staff for Continuity
body: Linnebur Electric, Inc. is owned and operated by the Linnebur family. We keep a smaller staff so there is continuity between projects and competency among employees, and everyone routinely attends continuing education classes.
Three of us are Master Electricians with at least 25 years of experience. We are licensed and insured, and our license number is #1353.

sections.heading: Offices, Restaurants, Churches and Clinics

sections.heading: Grain Elevators, Machine Shops and Truck Repair Facilities
body: Industrial jobs range from grain elevators and machine shops to truck repair facilities, and include metal building wiring, 3-phase motor control, grain handling facilities, CNC mill machine wiring and design/build work.
We enjoy getting out of town to work on agricultural projects, and we have done work in many of the areas around Wichita.

Our industrial staff is committed to communicating with customers to complete jobs in a timely manner, without sacrificing quality. If you're worried about distance, give us a call and see what we can do for you.

footer.about: Linnebur Electric, Inc. is a family-owned and operated electrical contractor in Wichita. We wire and repair homes, commercial buildings and industrial sites.

why: Your current site is four pages. The homepage headline is just “LINNEBUR ELECTRIC,” with no electrician and no Wichita, and every service sits on one page with the commercial and industrial lists hidden until someone taps. On a phone, the first screen has no phone number, and the Call button is inside the menu.

Your reviews say more than your site does. One customer wrote that you were the only guys who could find the problem and get it fixed, and another called you open, honest and responsive. Those words sit on Google, not on your site.

So the demo tells one story: when a problem has been hard to find, you find it. It opens with electrician in Wichita, KS, and gives electrical repair and outdoor lighting a page each. Your site prints License #1353 in the footer, so we kept it.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the Electrician People Find on Google
strategy.cardsIntro: Each card is one page of the demo.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: Where Google learns who you are and where you work.
problems: Your homepage headline and title say “Linnebur Electric,” with no electrician and no Wichita, so Google can't tell what you are or where.
Your services are one page, with the lists collapsed on a phone.
fixes: A headline that says electrician in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
The services laid out on the homepage, residential first, then commercial and industrial.
cards.alsoAdd: On day one, we sit down with you to get what makes you the obvious choice, every service you offer and every town you work in. From that we plan how many pages, in how many towns, so Google and AI tools can find you for every service.

cards.title: Electrical Repair
cards.why: When an outlet quits or a breaker won't stay on, people call the first electrician they find.
problems: “Service Work” is one line in a list, so “electrical repair Wichita KS” has nothing built for it.
The site doesn't say what you do when someone else's fix didn't hold.
fixes: A page for electrical repair in Wichita, KS, built on what customers wrote and what Linnebur's site lists.
Garage and shed outlets, older houses and commercial buildings answered on the page.
cards.alsoAdd: Outlet Installation, Ceiling Fan Installation and LED Lighting Retro-Fits pages, plus commercial and industrial pages, each built for its own search.

cards.title: Outdoor Lighting Installation
cards.why: People planning a backyard or pool area search for who to hire.
problems: Outdoor lighting isn't named anywhere on your site, though a customer hired you for lights around a pool and backyard.
“LED Lighting Retro-Fits” is a line in a list.
fixes: A page for outdoor lighting installation in Wichita, KS, built on one customer's pool and backyard job, with a tag to confirm it's offered.
LED retro-fits and exterior commercial work on the same page.

cards.title: Contact
cards.why: Where a customer with a dead outlet decides to call.
problems: Your contact page has no form and no hours, so someone who can't call has no way to ask.
On desktop, the phone number at the top of the page isn't a link.
fixes: Your address, number, email and what to have ready on one page.
Your number in the first screen, one tap away on a phone.

closing.heading: Want a website like this for your business?
closing.text: Your customers already describe the company you are. Book a strategy call with Fluid Frame and we'll walk you through this demo and what a full build adds.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your homepage says “over 30 years” while your about page says “Since 1982,” so which one should every listing use?
Your footer reads “LINNEBUR ELETRIC,” your logo reads “LINNEBUR ELECTRIC INC.” and your pages say “Linnebur Electric, Inc.,” so which name should Google and every directory show?
BBB lists Kent Linnebur as president and your site gives his email, while a Google review thanks “Rod and his crew,” so who should the site name as the person customers reach?

lead.heading: Why we led with finding the problem
lead.text: We led with finding the cause because it lives only in your reviews. One customer wrote that you were the only electricians who could find a problem several others couldn't, and a generic electrician page can't copy that.
